newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolan army said to move arms to interior.
newsitem.headline: Angolan army said to move arms to interior.

text.p: Angola's army, apparently bracing for rebel attacks, is moving large amounts of military hardware to the interior, air cargo workers, aid officials and diplomats said on Monday.

"I have been working in this business in Angola for almost 10 years and I have never seen so much military hardware moved around by the government as I have in the last two months," one air cargo employee said.

He said he had seen tanks, armoured personnel carriers, anti-aircraft guns as well as small arms, including rocket-propelled grenades, loaded in Luanda and unloaded in government-controlled cities in the interior.
The employee said the cities included Cafunfo, Nzaji and Saurimo, in the diamond-rich northeast, and the cities of Uige and Malange in the north.

Since the signing of a peace agreement between the government and the rebel movement UNITA, the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola, in 1994, Angola has enjoyed its longest period of peace since before independence from Portugal in 1975.

But recently the peace process has threatened to come unravelled. In May and June the government launched an offensive into UNITA zones in the northeast, in what military officials say is the biggest such operation since 1994.
More recently UNITA has failed to abide by United Nations demands to continue demilitarising and to allow the extension of government administration to the vast area under its control.
The former rebels' stance has triggered warnings by the U.N. Security Council that it will slap UNITA with additional sanctions if it does not comply by mid-August.

But UNITA's reluctance to move forward on the issues has also prompted the government to heighten its preparedness for a possible conflict with the former rebels, diplomats and military officials said.
Aid workers in the cities of Uige and in Malange report a large buildup of government military in the cities and frequent armed convoys and transport flights arriving in the cities.
Both Uige and Malange are surrounded by UNITA-held territory and would be obvious targets of the former rebels in case of a renewal of war.
"There are soldiers everywhere in Uige and there are constant army and police patrols in and around the city. People are very nervous up there," said one aid worker.
"The government is obviously getting ready," a diplomat said.
"It is beefing up its defence of vulnerable cities surrounded by UNITA and it is positioning itself for a possible attack on places most important to UNITA, such as the highland cities and Lusamba."

UNITA has its headquarters in the highland city of Bailundo and UNITA chief Jonas Savimbi lives in the nearby city of Andulo. Lusamba, in the northeast, is the centre of UNITA's lucrative diamond region where some 65 percent of the movement's estimated $700 million in annual diamond production is generated.
